raw_response.printed_headline_estimate: Table 4 (PDF p. 16 / p. 339, OLS, N = 631 LGA-ethnic state units, ethnicity-clustered SEs): Flush toilet access on precolonial Centralization = 0.039 (SE = 0.019, p < 0.05, col. 3); in col. 4, Centralization = 0.059 (SE = 0.026, p < 0.05), Supermajority muslim = -0.042 (SE = 0.030, NS), and Cent x S.Mus (indirect-rule hegemonization / 1976 Local Government Reform Law noncompliance) = -0.055 (SE = 0.029, p < 0.10). Table 5 (PDF p. 17 / p. 340, N = 631): null Centralization effects on locally administered Latrine (0.008, SE = 0.045, col. 2), Piped water (0.014, SE = 0.037, col. 4), and Tubewell water (0.079, SE = 0.060, col. 6). Table 7 (PDF p. 18 / p. 341, LGA-level OLS, N = 135-160 LGAs in Table 3; exact N omitted in Table 7): Pit Latrine access on Local government health standards = 0.170 (SE = 0.054, p < 0.01), Local government cleaning = 0.132 (SE = 0.048, p < 0.01), Local government marketplace = 0.183 (SE = 0.058, p < 0.01), Trust in local governing council = 0.127 (SE = 0.072, p < 0.10); Flush Toilet access = -0.141 (SE = 0.050, p < 0.01), -0.124 (SE = 0.049, p < 0.05), -0.193 (SE = 0.044, p < 0.01), and -0.214 (SE = 0.052, p < 0.01), respectively; Piped Water = 0.013 (SE = 0.040) to 0.030 (SE = 0.036), all NS.
raw_response.publication_year_note: Both the online-first date ('Published online: 03 Jan 2018', PDF p. 1) and the journal volume/issue year ('2018, VOL. 46, NO. 3, 325-347', PDF pp. 1-2; copyright 2018) are 2018; only the DOI string (10.1080/13600818.2017.1416072) contains 2017.
raw_response.rationale: Full text (24 pages) empirically estimates OLS regressions with robust/clustered standard errors linking intergovernmental administrative structure, local government institutional capacity, and historical indirect-rule/statutory governance arrangements to household water and sanitation access (DHS 1990-2013). Specifically: (1) Table 7 (PDF p. 18) tests LGA institutional/regulatory capacity (maintaining restaurant health standards, community cleaning, marketplace maintenance, and council trust) on locally administered Pit Latrine and Piped Water access versus federally administered Flush Toilet access, finding positive significant effects on Pit Latrine access (beta = 0.127* to 0.183***), null effects on Piped Water, and negative effects on Flush Toilet access (Family C: institutional-capacity/administrative-structure); and (2) Tables 4-5 (PDF pp. 16-17, N = 631 LGA-ethnic state partitions) test precolonial political centralization and indirect-rule hegemonization/noncompliance with the 1976 Local Government Reform Law (Cent x S.Mus) across federally administered Flush toilets (beta = 0.059**, interaction = -0.055*) versus locally administered Latrines, Piped water, and Tubewells (all null), bridging Family C (federal vs. LGA administrative structure) and Family A (indirect-rule vs. statutory governance arrangement).
